meta.title: Budlum Leaf part allocation under the Split, by distance class
meta.revision: L.7 candidate study, block HP-3, seat parts, 2026-10-19
meta.tags: Every mass marked derived, and every cost marked hypothesis, is [HYPOTHESIS]. Stated masses are [TREE] copies of the cited file.

codes.P: must stay in the Leaf: physics, law or an order of Ayaz
codes.S: stays on the Leaf by design: it can move only with a Leaf redesign, or moving it gains nothing
codes.M: can move to a Core (the frac field says how much of the part moves)
codes.A: added by the Split at that class
codes.W: in an older catalogue and not in the L.6.0 design, so it counts for nothing
codes.D: a dock part: it is not on the Leaf

classes.C0: contact or tether, up to 2 m: the maximum Split, under the rule of necessity. The radio SiPs move whole (upper bound)
classes.C0R: C0 with the radio SiPs kept (lower bound of the line item L3). Ayaz named the antennas and the 5G modem as staying
classes.C1: a room, up to about 30 m, with the stream of Part 21 (compressed slices, decoder on the Leaf)
classes.C2: far, up to kilometres: the Skin is the L.6.0 Leaf

meta.rule: Ayaz, 2026-10-19. A part stays in the B module only if physics forces it at the distance class. The body keeps the emitters and the tile drivers. Everything else is Core.

line_items.title: energy at C1 and C2
line_items.rule: The ruling lists no energy part, so the rule says Core.
line_items.held: Cells, TCMs, mux, B cell, coil and rectifier stay at C1 and C2. They move at C0.
line_items.why: Physics: watts do not cross 30 m or a kilometre. Brief section 8 item 4 says energy is local at C2.

line_items.title: the Buffer store at C0
line_items.rule: All 128 cells are Core at C0.
line_items.held: The table sends all 128 cells to the Core. The sensitivity keeps 20 cells: 2.4 g with their TCMs and the mux, about 12 USD at 1 M.
line_items.why: Law, not physics: the Host Life Law (Part 22, condition 4) asks for a bridge store at a host swap. Without it the Skin goes dark for 3 s.

line_items.title: the radio SiPs at C0
line_items.rule: The antennas and the radio front end stay. The baseband is Core.
line_items.held: U2A, U2B and U5 hold front end and baseband in one SiP. C0 moves them whole (upper bound). C0R keeps them whole (lower bound).
line_items.why: Physics keeps the front end at the antenna. No part list splits the SiP, so the truth lies between C0 and C0R.

line_items.title: the safe-screen ROM
line_items.rule: The compositor U1 is Core at C0, and its ROM with it.
line_items.held: A ROM-only die N02 stays on the Skin.
line_items.why: Law, not physics: every fault ends in a visible state (FINAL/08 8.2). Without it a link loss gives a dark Skin.

line_items.title: identity
line_items.rule: A hardened identity element stays at C1 and C2.
line_items.held: U7 stays at C1 and C2. At C0 the small chip N01 holds the identity and the part records, and the wallet moves to the Core.
line_items.why: The identity must stay (BRIEF section 4 item 4). The dead-pad law needs a verifier on the Skin.

line_items.title: touch front end, hinge and seam sensors, tile hubs
line_items.rule: The body keeps the emitters and the tile drivers only.
line_items.held: The touch front ends and the sensors stay. The tile hubs and seat controllers stay as tile drivers and link end.
line_items.why: Physics: an electrode or a strain sensor is read at the tile, because a long trace adds noise and delay. Scan logic can move.

line_items.title: the 36.2 C hardware cut-off
line_items.rule: Not an emitter or a tile driver, so Core.
line_items.held: The NTCs and the comparator stay in the body.
line_items.why: Physics and law: a surface temperature is measured at the surface, and the cut-off acts with the link lost (ENR-16).

line_items.title: the IMU
line_items.rule: Not in the list of the ruling, so Core.
line_items.why: Physics: it senses the seat, the face and the grip of the Leaf. A Core IMU senses the Core.

line_items.title: audio codec, power chip, boot NOR, rail parts
line_items.rule: Not in the list, so Core.
line_items.held: U3, U4, U9, U4B and the rail inductors stay in the module.
line_items.why: Physics: the DAC and amplifier sit at the speaker and jack, and the camera, panel and flash rails are local. U4 also answers the dead-pad law. U9 holds the firmware of the stayers.

line_items.title: heat parts of the camera
line_items.rule: Not in the list, so Core.
line_items.held: The spreader, phase change buffer, Cu-graphite shield and graphite shield stay.
line_items.why: Physics: the camera and the emitters make heat where they are. The buffer was sized for the camera sentinel, so it can shrink after the move (candidate K-1).

line_items.title: the seat interface and the dead-pad law
line_items.rule: Not an emitter or a tile driver, so Core.
line_items.held: The seat fields, seam leaves, 12 bar leaves and the ring serdes stay.
line_items.why: Law and physics: the 12 leaves are the only wired seat and the tether interface at C0. The dead-pad responder must sit at the pads (ENR-19).

line_items.title: the camera encoder and the uplink
line_items.rule: Sentinel work is processing, so Core.
line_items.held: At C1 and C2 the encoder in U6 stays. At C0 it moves if a display pair is switched to uplink.
line_items.why: Physics: the uplink under SAR is weak, and 12.5 MP at 30 fps needs 3.75 Gbit/s. Only compressed video crosses a room or a kilometre.

parts.n: PC caps, hard coat, AgNW touch grid
parts.ms: derived: 12800 mm2 x 0.25 mm x 1.20 g/cm3 (F21 21.2.7, density from meta)
parts.why: The cap is the touch surface and the hard coat. Touch sensing is physics.

parts.n: optical adhesive, cap to glass
parts.why: A layer of the tile stack. It leaves with no part above or below it.

parts.n: micro-LED layer: 5.12 M chips, 1.28 M pixel uICs, TGV glass
parts.ms: derived: 12800 mm2 x 0.25 mm x 2.45 g/cm3 (F21 21.2.7, DR)
parts.why: The emitters at 50 um pitch and their uICs. Light must be made at the surface.

parts.n: tile hub die: DSC decode, demura, 4 retimed ports
parts.ms: derived: 3 x 3 x 0.1 mm die and package, hypothesis (DR open issue 5)
parts.today: coil or spreader layer of each tile
parts.why: Each tile latches its 105 Mbit/s packets locally. This is the minimal decoder of the Skin.

parts.n: slip OCA between glass and coil layer
parts.why: A layer of the tile stack, so it stays with the tile.

parts.n: Qi2.2 sector coils x4, ferrite and Mu-metal shield, NP0 bank
parts.ms: STU mass_and_stack qi_g 3.0 [HYPOTHESIS]; H17 group 9 states 3.2 g with Q-local coils
parts.today: 0.20 mm coil layer, ring of about 45 mm
parts.why: Rule of necessity: at C0 the tether carries power, so the coil is not forced. The Skin omits it and the Core charges itself. At C1 and C2 energy is local, so it stays.

parts.n: U_Q x4 rectifier and 3:1 charger
parts.why: It goes with the coil at C0. At C1 and C2 it feeds the local cells from the seat field and the coil.

parts.n: hermetic micro cells, 9.25 x 9.25 x 0.90 mm, 30 um can
parts.ms: CS: 0.115 g (G) or 0.114 g (S) per cell, times 128
parts.refs: H15 #1-4, H17 group 7 (LLZO pouch, withdrawn by F21 21.1)
parts.today: 0.90 mm cell layer of every tile
parts.why: Energy is not forced at C0, so all 128 cells go. At C1 and C2 power does not travel 30 m (BR 8.4), so they stay. Buffer: line item L2.

parts.n: TCM protection IC, fuse and balance channel per cell
parts.ms: derived: 128 dies at about 2 mg, hypothesis (F21 21.2.5)
parts.why: It follows its cell.

parts.n: floating back skin, TPU or silicone, 0.08 mm
parts.today: back face, bonded to tile-centre pads
parts.why: The outer surface of the stretching body.

parts.n: edge-on polyimide hinges (232), copper and EGaIn lanes, routing layer
parts.ms: derived: ribbon volume is about 3 mm3, routing copper dominates, hypothesis (F21 21.2.2, DI section C)
parts.why: The hinge is the stretch mechanism and carries the 13 display lines.

parts.n: Ti hub, 8 Ti pins, 24 N52H magnets, kinematic seat balls and vees
parts.today: the plus crossing and the quadrant lines
parts.why: The quadrant seat is mechanical. L.6.0 changed its parts, so the stated mass is a reference only.

parts.n: seam lip and plus seam optical lip
parts.why: The seam is part of the face.

parts.n: four seat fields: 12 gold lands per edge, keepers, dead-pad pad, first-break pad, gasket land, moisture pad
parts.why: The contact interface of the bar, the port part and the Core plug. The dead-pad law lives here.

parts.n: 64 seam gold leaves and 4 dead-pad switches
parts.why: They join the quadrants. L.6.0 turns them into split couplers, so the mass is a reference.

parts.n: graphite spreader and Mu-metal ocular shield
parts.ms: derived: shares the 0.20 mm layer with the coil (F21 21.2.7); H16 group 6 states 3.4 g (L.5.0)
parts.why: It spreads heat at the eye. The 36.2 C limit is a surface fact.

parts.n: 36.2 C ocular NTC limiter with hardware comparator
parts.why: A hardware cut-off must act at the surface in every class. A link cannot carry it.

parts.n: AgNW touch front end per tile, scan at 480 Hz
parts.ms: derived: 128 small dies, hypothesis (F21 21.5.5, E03 section 1.1)
parts.why: Touch sensing is physics. Scan results can travel, the electrodes cannot.

parts.n: hinge-angle sensor, seam capacitive strip, thermistor per tile
parts.ms: derived: small sensors, hypothesis (F21 21.2.4, E03 section 1.1)
parts.why: Physical sensors of the closed loops. The loop logic can move, the sensor cannot.

parts.n: seat controller and edge router, one per seat tile
parts.why: The link end of the Skin. It receives the pixel pairs and routes them over the hinge mesh.

parts.n: ultrasonic edge weld, IP67 seal, edge gasket lands
parts.ms: derived: H14 #13 states 0.06 g for the gasket land, weld bead added, hypothesis
parts.why: The seal is a property of the surface.

parts.n: body antennas A5, A6 (5G slots), A7 (GNSS), A8 (NFC loop) in AgNW
parts.ms: no mass stated; the conductors are in the AgNW layer (H19 section 2). F21 does not restate A5 to A8
parts.today: tile perimeter and the plus crossing
parts.why: Antennas as designed stay. Part 21 names no A5 to A8, which is an open item.

parts.n: Qi alignment magnets (16 N52 in tile corners) and QI2_AC_RING seam leaves
parts.ms: H14 #4 (0.52 g, L.5.0 ring arcs; F21 21.2.6 item 5 gives 16 magnets) and #6 (0.16 g)
parts.today: chamfered tile corners and quadrant lines
parts.why: Part of the Qi path. It leaves with the coil at C0 and stays at C1 and C2.

parts.n: bar shell with the moulded 90 degree corner
parts.why: It carries the antennas as designed. The order of Ayaz keeps the bar.

parts.n: A1 inverted-F and A2 coupled arm, LDS copper
parts.why: Antennas as designed. The Core cannot hold them.

parts.n: A4 1x4 60 GHz patch array
parts.why: Antenna as designed. A large Core array adds gain on its own end.

parts.n: 12 gold body-link leaves over the seat tile
parts.why: The one wired interface of the Leaf. At C0 it is the tether interface.

parts.n: corner flex, 20 lines, through the moulded bend
parts.why: It feeds the bar antennas from the ring. At C0 its antenna lines end in no radio.

parts.n: ring shell, LCP-GF40
parts.why: It houses the camera, panel, audio and jack that stay. Shrinking it is a Leaf redesign.

parts.n: front sapphire window, camera L1
parts.why: The lens stays with the sensor (BR 4.3).

parts.n: rear sapphire window
parts.why: Window of the rear panel.

parts.n: rear round LTPO AMOLED, 480 x 480
parts.why: An emitter on the back of the Leaf. Its stream can come over the link at C0.

parts.n: Cu-graphite shield between camera and rear panel
parts.why: It guards the sensor from the panel. The camera stays.

parts.n: 50 MP camera column, f/2.0, 0.12 mm focus, in-plane stabiliser
parts.why: Lens, sensor, focus and stabiliser must sit at the view. The column sets the 4.00 mm floor.

parts.n: LED flash, two colour temperatures
parts.why: An emitter. Light is made where the scene is.

parts.n: micro-speaker
parts.why: A transducer at the user. A Core 2 m away is not at the ear.

parts.n: two MEMS microphones, ePTFE mesh
parts.why: Transducers at the mouth. They stay with the Leaf.

parts.n: ring PCBA, 8-layer HDI
parts.why: It still routes the camera, panel, audio and jack. A smaller board is a candidate for Ayaz.

parts.n: U1 TCON and local compositor (safe-screen ROM inside)
parts.why: At C0 the compositor is not forced and moves. At C1 and C2 the rule keeps it. Its safe-screen ROM needs a Skin stub (N02).

parts.n: U2A Wi-Fi 7 and BT 6.0 combo
parts.today: ring PCBA, under a shield can
parts.why: One SiP holds the front end and the baseband. The front end stays, the baseband can move: line item L3. At C1 and C2 it is the link PHY.

parts.n: U2B 60 GHz and UWB
parts.today: ring PCBA, under a shield can
parts.why: One SiP holds the front end and the baseband: line item L3. At C1 and C2 it is the link PHY and the UWB ranging.

parts.n: U5 5G standalone modem with RF front end and eSIM
parts.today: ring PCBA, under a shield can
parts.why: One SiP holds the front end and the baseband: line item L3. Ayaz named the 5G modem as staying. The eSIM moves with it at C0.

parts.n: U6 slice decoder, camera encoder block and 16 MB frame store
parts.ms: H13 #20; encoder block named in PL as U6 codec
parts.why: At C0 decoder and store are not forced. At C1 and C2 the rule keeps them. The encoder needs an uplink lane at C0.

parts.n: U7 secure element: wallet keys, validator set, receipts
parts.today: ring PCBA, always-on from the B cell
parts.why: At C0 a Skin identity chip replaces it (N01). At C1 and C2 it is the hardened identity element and the wallet.

parts.n: U8 IMU
parts.why: It senses the seat, the face and the grip of the Leaf. A Core IMU senses the Core.

parts.n: U3 audio codec and U4 power chip with dead-pad switch
parts.why: The codec sits at the jack and speaker. U4 regulates the camera, panel and flash rails and answers the dead-pad law.

parts.n: A3 ring loop, LDS copper
parts.today: ring rim, around the jack groove
parts.why: Antenna as designed. It is the second Wi-Fi antenna of the 2 x 2 pair.

parts.n: aperture tuners, three switched networks
parts.today: ring PCBA, at the antenna feeds
parts.why: A tuner sits at the feed of an antenna that stays. It idles at C0.

parts.n: 3.5 mm jack in the ring rim
parts.why: A connector for a plug at the Leaf. Order of Ayaz.

parts.n: cell multiplexer, 4 x 32 channels
parts.why: It watches the 128 cells and goes with them at C0. At C1 and C2 it stays with the cells.

parts.n: 8 N52H seat magnets in the sliding pad
parts.ms: H13 #28 (0.34 g; H14 #32 states 1.55 g for the same 8 magnets)
parts.why: The ring holds to the face by magnets.

parts.n: B cell, 0.14 Wh, 20 x 8 x 1.50 mm
parts.today: ring PCBA, stacked over cold parts
parts.why: It is the island rail of the wallet and radios. At C0 power comes by tether and the Buffer cells bridge.

parts.n: FKM gaskets and the jack contact pocket
parts.why: The seal is a property of the ring.

parts.n: graphite spreader and 1.0 g phase change buffer
parts.why: The camera still makes heat. Shrinking the buffer needs a thermal re-run (heat seat). Candidate only.

parts.n: shield cans, nickel silver, over U2A, U2B, U5
parts.why: A can follows its SiP: line item L3.

parts.n: U9 boot NOR, 16 MiB
parts.ms: derived: 2.0 x 3.0 x 0.55 mm x 2.5 g/cm3 (PL parts); not in H13
parts.why: It holds the firmware of U3, U8 and the camera sequencer, which stay. FZ section 4.

parts.n: U4B bias and flash driver
parts.ms: derived: 2.0 x 2.0 x 0.40 mm x 2.5 g/cm3 (PL parts); not in H13
parts.why: It drives the flash and camera bias at the emitter.

parts.n: Y1 TCXO
parts.ms: derived: 2.0 x 1.6 x 0.70 mm x 2.5 g/cm3 (PL parts); not in H13
parts.why: It clocks the baseband and follows the SiPs: line item L3.

parts.n: Y2 32 kHz crystal
parts.ms: derived: 1.6 x 1.0 x 0.45 mm x 2.5 g/cm3 (PL parts); not in H13
parts.why: A real-time clock for the ring stub.

parts.n: inductors L1 to L7
parts.ms: derived: 7 x 2.0 x 1.25 x 0.65 mm x 4.0 g/cm3 (PL parts); not in H13
parts.why: Rail inductors of U4 and the camera and panel rails. Some serve moved chips, which a redesign can drop.

parts.n: camera flex and display flex
parts.ms: derived: 3.0 x 1.6 x 0.5 and 4.0 x 1.6 x 0.5 mm, hypothesis (PL parts); not in H13
parts.why: They connect the camera and the rear panel.

parts.n: Skin identity chip: pairing, part record (law L9), verify only, no signing key
parts.ms: derived: size of U7 (H13 #21); study seat prices it at 1.0 to 1.5 USD (STU)
parts.why: The identity must stay (BR 4). It answers the dead-pad challenge by verifying the Core and holds the part records.

parts.n: Skin safe-screen ROM die (the U1 ROM path kept on the Skin)
parts.ms: derived: small ROM-only die, hypothesis (FZ section 4: 256 KiB ROM and timing)
parts.why: The safe screen shows on a link loss in 60 ms. The session seat already assumes a ROM screen in 15 ms.

parts.n: ring serdes bridge for camera, rear panel, audio and IMU over the leaves
parts.why: The 12 leaves carry two display pairs and a 0.4 Gbit/s back channel. The ring streams need a bridge and a lane.

parts.n: USB-C receptacle, IP68, with strain relief
parts.ms: H14 #17 (0.85 g) and #37 (0.10 g); L.5.0 value reused for the L.6.0 port part [HYPOTHESIS]
parts.today: clip-on on a free body edge
parts.why: A separate product (F21 21.3.4). A Core tether at C0 can use the same clip-on family. Candidate.

parts.n: PD controller, inductor, filter, decoupling, ESD, redriver
parts.why: Power negotiation of the port part.

parts.n: 12 gold pogo pins and O-rings
parts.why: They mate with the 12 pads of a seat field.

parts.n: latch magnets x8 and orientation Hall sensor
parts.ms: H14 #32 (1.55 g) and #34 (0.02 g); 8 N52H of 3.2 x 1.6 x 1.1 mm weigh 0.34 g by volume
parts.why: Holds the clip-on to an edge.

parts.n: dead-pad authenticator, FKM skirt, potting
parts.why: The port part answers the dead-pad challenge as role port.

parts.n: RF and power isolation shield, regulatory plate, optional PORT-CJ and PORT-CA adapters
parts.ms: H14 #36 (0.17 g), #39 (0.05 g); #40 and #41 are optional accessories with no mass stated
parts.why: Support parts of the port part. L.5.0 values reused.

parts.n: dock complete, 240 x 120 x 12 mm class
parts.ms: H18 section 1 (310 g, or 360 g with the 45 TOPS board); L.5.0 figure, hw/dock/params.py redraws it
parts.why: A host for C0 contact. A Core at C0 can be built as the dock. Candidate.

parts.n: deck, seat land, Qi2.2 transmitter coil, pad set, pad springs, VESA mount, guide pins, feet
parts.ms: no part masses stated (H18 parts 1 to 9 and 23 to 25)
parts.why: The contact side of the dock.

parts.n: deck board, PD sink, Qi and pad power stage, 2.5 GbE PHY, switch
parts.ms: no part masses stated (H18 parts 10 to 15)
parts.why: The power and network side of the dock.

parts.n: regulated pad: AlN window, TEC, heat sink, blower
parts.why: The heat path of Part 22. The Skin load of 1.0 to 1.6 W passes only on a pulled heat path in still air.

parts.n: dock pack, 20 Wh, two pouch cells, and its protector
parts.ms: E05 section 2.1: 2 x 70 x 60 x 3.7 mm, no mass stated
parts.why: A near energy host for C0 contact. The Core can share it. Candidate.

parts.n: validator bay and 45 TOPS validator board (option), Wi-Fi 7 AP, 60 GHz radio, UWB anchor
parts.ms: H18 parts 14 and 17 to 20; hw/dock/params.py LOADS and VALIDATOR
parts.why: The room validator and radios. This is a C1 Core in all but name.

parts.n: dock secure element, serial plate, status bar, B module post
parts.why: Dock identity and the post for large members.

parts.n: LLZO/PEO pouch cells x4 with Al-laminate pouches and foil tabs
parts.ms: withdrawn by F21 21.1: 128 hermetic micro cells replace them
parts.why: Not in the L.6.0 design. The stated 68 g body still counts these cells.

parts.n: T-OLED panels x8 and ITO/AgNW mesh x8
parts.ms: withdrawn by F21 21.1: micro-LED tiles and AgNW
parts.why: Replaced by BD03 and BD01.

parts.n: PC shells x8 and OCA slip layers x8
parts.why: Replaced by the tile stack.

parts.n: PDLC privacy film x4
parts.ms: the 21.2.7 stack has no PDLC layer; Part 21 does not name it as withdrawn
parts.why: Open: not in the L.6.0 stack. The Split does not touch it.

parts.n: holdover capacitors x4 and local Qi coils x4
parts.ms: not in the 21.2.7 stack nor in 21.2.6 (four sector coils only)
parts.why: Open: Part 22 needs a hold-up path, and the stack has no room for these.

parts.n: L.5.0 stem, Ti hinge, USB-C, aluminium ring, folded camera, 0.45 Wh bridge cell
parts.ms: F21 21.1 replaces the module with the 32 parts of H13 (10.80 g)
parts.why: The 20 g and 22 g module figures are withdrawn.

parts.n: L.5.0 stem parts: Ti shells, Ti hinge barrel, hinge flex, stem board, headset codec and amplifier
parts.ms: withdrawn by F21 21.1 (stem and hinge) and by H13 (the codec is U3 in the ring)
parts.why: Not in the L.6.0 design.

collisions.title: the 50 MP camera column and the Core taking camera processing
collisions.where: CAM-21, MON-23, F21 21.3.5, M09 sections 3.1 and 3.2, CAM-3
collisions.what: The lens and sensor must stay. The sentinel (remosaic, compression, encode) needs an uplink. The leaves hold a 0.4 Gbit/s back channel, and 12.5 MP at 30 fps needs 3.75 Gbit/s.
collisions.C0: Zone 1 stays. Move the sentinel only if a display pair is switched to camera uplink in capture mode (HC-A5), or keep the encoder in U6.
collisions.C1: No change. The sentinel stays, because the uplink carries 30 to 80 Mbit/s of compressed video and 12 to 30 MB stills.
collisions.C2: No change. A weak uplink under SAR forbids raw video.

collisions.title: the 4.00 mm module is set by the camera column
collisions.what: Moving silicon frees area and volume in the ring. It does not thin the module, because the column stands 3.90 mm.
collisions.C0: Module stays 4.00 mm. Freed volume is room, not thickness.
collisions.C1: Nothing leaves the ring. Module stays 4.00 mm.
collisions.C2: Nothing leaves the ring. Module stays 4.00 mm.

collisions.title: camera state declaration and hardware indicator
collisions.what: A hardware indicator and a signed sensor declaration stop software from hiding camera use. U7 signs today. The Skin signs nothing.
collisions.C0: Wire the indicator to the sensor supply rail on the Skin. The Core signs the declaration and names the Skin identity (HC-A5).
collisions.C1: No change. U7 stays on the Leaf.

collisions.title: the 12 gold leaves and the one wired seat
collisions.where: MON-23, MON-18, MON-21, F21 21.3.2 and 21.3.3, E03 section 2
collisions.what: The leaves carry two display pairs, a 0.4 Gbit/s back channel, VBUS, VHV, sideband and ground. The ring slides on a stretching face and a cable pulls on the bar.
collisions.C0: A Core plug takes the leaves in place of the ring chips, or a port-part clip-on takes another edge. Test a 30 N pull on a seat (HC-A4).
collisions.C1: No change. The leaves carry the ring only.

collisions.title: the dead-pad law
collisions.where: ENR-19, MON-16, FS state PAD_AUTH, RL-7, RL-14
collisions.what: Every pad holds 0 V until a 3 ms challenge. The challenger verifies a signed answer. At C0 the answer comes from the Core, and the Skin holds no signing key.
collisions.C0: The Skin identity chip verifies the Core certificate in 3 ms. First break opens the FET in under 0.8 ms (HC-A4).
collisions.C1: Not used. No pad touches a Core. The pairing key of the trust seat replaces the challenge.
collisions.C2: Not used. The law holds on the bar and the port part as designed.

collisions.title: the Zero CPU definition
collisions.where: F21 21.5.1, F21 21.4.2, FZ section 4, naming law of BR section 7
collisions.what: Part 21 gives the Leaf no general-purpose processor and no operating system. The Core holds the validator role, which needs both.
collisions.C0: Relocated silicon stays fixed-function. Claim Zero CPU for the Skin and the relocated block. Name the validator role as a separate node (HC-A10).
collisions.C1: Same. A room validator is a node, as the dock validator is today.
collisions.C2: No change. The Core is a validator, not part of the Leaf.

collisions.title: the local compositor, the stretch warp and the Part 21 interaction budget
collisions.what: U1 moves cursor, scroll, glyph echo and the per-tile warp in under 10 ms. SW-23 needs a predicted action with the network cut.
collisions.C0: The Core runs the compositor. The tether round trip is well under 1 ms. SW-23 cuts the Core uplink, not the tether.
collisions.C1: Compositor stays on the Leaf, as the ruling of Ayaz says.
collisions.C2: No change. The far round trip is 80 ms, so the Leaf compositor and speculative frames are essential.

collisions.title: the stream check and the wallet on the Leaf
collisions.where: F21 21.5.4, F21 21.5.8, SW-22, BR section 4 item 4
collisions.what: U7 accepts a stream only from an active validator key. With U7 on the Core, the Skin trusts the paired Core key and nothing else.
collisions.C0: SW-22 moves to the Core. The Skin refuses an unpaired Core key. The rogue Skin reads every pixel (HC-A11).
collisions.C1: No change. U7 stays as the hardened identity element.

collisions.title: the safe-screen ROM lives in U1
collisions.where: FS (U1 ROM path), FINAL/08 section 8.2 safe-screen law, I2 (60 ms)
collisions.what: Every fault ends in a visible state. If U1 leaves and the link fails, the Skin is dark and the law is broken.
collisions.C0: Keep a ROM-only safe-screen die on the Skin (N02). Show it within 60 ms of a link loss (HC-A3).

collisions.title: the seam loop and the 3 ms recalibration after a swap
collisions.what: U1 shifts the image in 3.125 um steps and recalibrates in the 3 ms window. The calibration of 32 tiles is about 154 KB, so the back channel needs 3.1 ms.
collisions.C0: Read the calibration over a pair (0.2 ms), or keep the closed loop in the tile hubs (HC-A6).

collisions.title: frame store, decoder and compositor at C1 and C2
collisions.where: F21 21.5.1, BR section 8 item 2, DSC link of DI
collisions.what: Slices of tens to 150 Mbit/s cross a room. The raw stream of 6 to 12 Gbit/s needs the 60 GHz array, and Wi-Fi 7 2 x 2 tops out at 5.76 Gbit/s PHY.
collisions.C0: Not needed. The tether carries 13.43 Gbit/s over two pairs.
collisions.C1: U6, the frame store and the compositor stay. The ruling of Ayaz keeps them at C1 and C2. HC-A9 measures the link and confirms the necessity.
collisions.C2: U6 stays. No raw stream crosses a kilometre.

collisions.title: the radios and the antennas are one design
collisions.what: A1 to A4 are tuned to U2A and U2B with the tuners. A SiP holds the front end and the baseband together. Ayaz keeps the antennas and the 5G modem on the Leaf.
collisions.C0: The rule keeps the front end and moves the baseband, which no part list splits. C0 moves the SiPs whole. C0R keeps them. The truth lies between.
collisions.C1: All three radios stay. They are the Leaf end of the link.

collisions.title: dormant antennas and a Leaf that cannot roam at C0
collisions.where: BR section 8, F21 21.4.1, RF-21 to RF-23
collisions.what: If the radios move, the bar antennas and the corner flex lines end in no radio. A Skin off its tether is then dark. An RF cable of 2 m loses many dB at 60 GHz.
collisions.C0: Choose C0R (radios stay), or accept a tether-only Skin. The choice is for Ayaz (candidate K-3).
collisions.C1: No change. The antennas feed the radios on the Leaf.

collisions.title: Qi2.2 on a Skin with no cell behind it
collisions.what: At C0 the tether carries power, so the rule omits the coil, the rectifier and the alignment magnets. A Skin that must charge off its tether needs them.
collisions.C0: The Skin omits the Qi path (3.9 g). The Core charges its own cells. Candidate K-2 puts it back.
collisions.C1: No change. Energy is local, so the coil stays.

collisions.title: Article 11, the removable quadrant and the Buffer rule
collisions.where: FINAL/17 17.6, F22 22.12, E06 section 2, ENR-13, ENR-22
collisions.what: The quadrant is the user battery today: 32 cells, TCMs, U_Q and bonded tiles. With all cells in the Core, Article 11 applies to the Core battery.
collisions.C0: The Core cells need tool-free removal. The Skin quadrant holds no cell and is display only (HC-A6).
collisions.C1: No change. Cells stay in the quadrants.

collisions.title: the legal class of the Leaf
collisions.where: E06 section 1 (2023/1670 class with modem and voice path)
collisions.what: The Leaf sits in a regulation class because it has a 5G modem and a voice path. A Skin with no modem can fall outside it, and the Core can enter it.
collisions.C0: Ask a lawyer which box is the product. Hypothesis only.

collisions.title: the mass figures of the catalogues
collisions.what: The stated 68 g body counts 34.4 g of withdrawn LLZO cells. The L.6.0 body has no mass list. The 88 g total counts a withdrawn 20 g module.
collisions.C0: State the mass of Skin, Core and tether as three configurations (the mass rule of FINAL/03 3.1).
collisions.C1: State Leaf and Core mass as two configurations.

collisions.title: the rear display and wallet standby with no Core
collisions.where: E04 section 3 (rear glance 75 min, wallet standby 143 min on the B cell), E05 section 1.3 rule 5
collisions.what: At C0 the rear glance, the clock and the wallet standby need the Core, because U1, U7 and the B cell leave.
collisions.C0: The Skin alone shows the safe screen only. State it in the product text.
collisions.C1: No change. The B cell, U1 and U7 stay.

collisions.title: the Host Life Law and a Skin with no store
collisions.where: F22 22.2 condition 4, F22 D-9, HST-1, HST-2, HST-5
collisions.what: Part 22 asks for a bridge store, so a host swap loses no session. The rule of necessity sends all cells to the Core at C0.
collisions.C0: Line item L2. Keep 20 Buffer cells (2.4 g) or accept a dark Skin for 3 s at a host swap. Ayaz decides (K-7).

gates.test: the allocation table against the catalogues
gates.pass: Each part of HARDWARE/13 (32 rows) and each group of HARDWARE/14 to 19 has one cited row. parts.py exits 0. The module sum is 10.80 g within 0.01 g.

gates.test: the ring after the move, by area and by packing
gates.pass: At C0 the staying ring parts fill 60 percent or less of the free board area. The packer places every part with 0 errors.

gates.test: the safe screen with the link cut or the Core off
gates.pass: At C0 the Skin shows the ROM safe screen within 60 ms of a link loss. No updatable code is on the path. 65 536 fault sets pass.

gates.test: the Core plug on a seat: dead-pad law, first break and pull
gates.pass: Pads stay at 0 V until the 3 ms answer. First break opens the FET in under 0.8 ms under a 30 N side pull. 1 000 mates, no damage.
A display pair switched to uplink carries 12.5 MP at 60 fps (7.5 Gbit/s) with no dropped frame. The hardware indicator follows the sensor rail, with no software path.

gates.test: the quadrant swap on a Skin with no cells
gates.pass: Swap under 3 s. The calibration of 32 tiles loads in under 3 ms. Core cells leave with no tool in under 30 s.

gates.test: the part record on the Core and the Skin identity chip
gates.pass: Every moved part carries a record on the Core. The identity chip signs challenges only and holds no wallet key. A mismatched Core and Skin pair is refused.
Each part is weighed (MEC-2). The Skin mass at C0 is within 10 percent of out/summary.txt. The weighed Leaf replaces the 68 g and 88 g figures.

gates.test: the necessity test at C1: decoder, store and compositor
gates.pass: The 60 GHz array measured at 30 m for 1 h gives under 13.43 Gbit/s. That confirms the rule. A higher rate goes to Ayaz and no part moves.

gates.test: the Zero CPU and naming claims
gates.pass: No text calls a Core that hosts the validator role Zero CPU. The word Leaf names the Skin. A search for the banned product names returns 0 hits.

gates.test: the stream check on the Skin
gates.pass: A stream from an unpaired Core key shows the safe screen in 1 000 of 1 000 trials. A rogue Skin gets no key.

gates.test: the antennas at C0 and C0R
gates.pass: In C0R the gates RF-21 to RF-23 pass unchanged. In C0 the antennas keep their return loss with the radios removed, and the Leaf states that it cannot roam.

gates.test: the host swap on a Skin with no store (line item L2)
gates.pass: The Skin shows the safe screen through a 3 s host swap and resumes. If not, the 20-cell Buffer is added and HST-2 passes.

candidates.text: Shrink the ring board and the spreader after the C0 move, to buy thickness or a larger camera sensor. It needs a Leaf redesign.
Put the Qi coil, rectifier and magnets (3.9 g) back on the C0 Skin, if it must charge off its tether.
Choose C0 or C0R for the radio SiPs. C0R keeps 1.0 g and 54 USD on the Leaf at 1 M a year, plus the 61 USD royalty.
Build the C0 Core as the dock family. The dock already holds the pad, the heat path, the 20 Wh pack and the validator bay.
Add a mass list of the L.6.0 body to HARDWARE, and retire the 68 g and 88 g figures.
Delete the cell layer from all 128 tiles at C0. The tile stack falls from 2.00 mm to 1.10 mm, or 0.90 mm without the coil layer.
Keep 20 Buffer cells on the C0 Skin for the Host Life Law. They weigh 2.4 g with their TCMs and the mux, hold 0.9 to 1.2 Wh and cost about 12 USD at 1 M.
